sections.h2: Who collects and who assesses property tax in Nelson County, Kentucky?
sections.html:
The Nelson County Sheriff's Office collects the tax, and the Nelson County Property Valuation Administration (PVA) sets the value. The sheriff's page is blunt about the split: the sheriff never assesses property, so a bill that looks wrong goes to the PVA at (502) 348-1810.

The sheriff collects for the state, the county and the school districts, and sometimes for cities and special districts when a contract exists. That means the bill a Nelson County owner receives depends on where the house sits. The sheriff's page lists which bills each magisterial district receives.

  • Districts 1, 7, 8, 11, 12 and 13: a county bill only.
  • District 2: a county bill and a City of New Haven bill.
  • District 3: county schools and City of Bardstown bills.
  • District 4: county, Bardstown city and Bardstown Independent School bills.
  • District 5: county and Bardstown Independent School bills.
  • District 9: county and City of Fairfield bills.

A seller should look at the bill in hand and confirm that every line has been paid, because a house in the Bardstown district can carry more than one bill.

sections.h2: What is Nelson County like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Nelson County was the fourth county created in what is now Kentucky, formed from Jefferson County in 1784. It covers about 418 square miles of land, and the county seat, Bardstown, is among the oldest cities in Kentucky and counted 13,567 residents in 2020. The county is known for bourbon, and Bardstown markets itself as the Bourbon Capital of the World, with Heaven Hill, Barton 1792, Willett and Lux Row among the distilleries in and around town.

The county sheriff patrols Bardstown, Bloomfield, New Haven, Fairfield, Boston, Chaplin and New Hope, so a seller can be in a city or in open country within a few miles. Bardstown sits where U.S. 31E, U.S. 62 and U.S. 150 meet, and the Bluegrass Parkway runs just south of the city. The Nelson County micropolitan area belongs to the Louisville combined statistical area.

Two public districts serve the county, Nelson County Schools and Bardstown City Schools, and the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Louisville runs several parochial schools. One oddity is that Nelson County High School stands inside the Bardstown district's boundary, so a buyer who cares about schools should check which district a particular address belongs to.

sections.h2: How do Nelson County housing numbers compare with the rest of the area?
sections.html:
Census QuickFacts describes a growing county. The population estimate for July 2025 is 49,036, up 4.9% from the 2020 base, and 63.0% of residents 16 and older are in the labor force.

  • Housing units, 2025 estimate: 21,097, with 222 building permits issued in 2025.
  • Owner-occupied rate, 2020 to 2024: 78.3%.
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $238,000.
  • Median monthly owner costs: $1,379 with a mortgage and $473 without.
  • Median gross rent: $1,008.
  • Median household income: $69,562, with 11.7% of people in poverty.

About 90.3% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, and 23.8% of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree. With 222 permits in a year, a resale competes with new construction.

sections.h2: When are Nelson County property taxes due, and what do the penalties add?
sections.html:
Nelson's sheriff posts the same four-step schedule that KRS 134.015 sets for Kentucky. The discount ends on November 1, the face amount is due through December 31, and penalties start in January.

Nelson County bill amounts by payment date
Payment dateAmount
On or before November 12% discount
November 2 to December 31Face amount
January 1 to January 315% penalty
February 1 to April 1521% penalty

Bills not paid to the sheriff by April 15 are handled by the County Clerk. The sheriff stresses that the payment must match the bill exactly. A check for the wrong amount is returned, as is any late or partial payment, so confirm the figure for the day you pay before you write the check.

sections.h2: What does an unpaid Nelson County bill cost?
sections.html:
Because values here run higher, the dollars add up faster. On a $2,500 bill, the discount price is $2,450 and the face amount is $2,500. January brings it to $2,625, and the February to April 15 period makes it $3,025, which is $575 more than the discount price.

If a mortgage company escrows your tax, send them the bill. The sheriff's page says the first proper payment received is the one processed, and no refund is issued to an owner who pays ahead of the lender. A seller closing in winter should ask the lender whether the escrow payment has already gone out before sending a second check.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Nelson County assessment?
sections.html:
Go to the PVA first. Under KRS 133.120, any owner who wants to contest a real property value must request a conference with the PVA or a deputy, either before or during the inspection period. The statute lets the owner hold that conference by phone.

The tax roll is open for 13 days starting the first Monday in May, according to KRS 133.045. An owner who is still aggrieved files a written petition with the County Clerk, naming the property, giving reasons and stating the fair cash value, no later than one workday after the inspection period ends. The county board of assessment appeals sets a hearing, and the owner must bring facts, such as sales listings, an appraisal, insurance policies or construction costs.

No appeal delays the due date. Pay on the value you claimed, and an increase after appeal is billed with interest from the original due date. Anyone who does not appear before the county board loses the right to go directly to the state Board of Tax Appeals.

sections.h2: Is the Kentucky homestead exemption available in Nelson County?
sections.html:
Yes, to owners who are 65 or older or classed as totally disabled. The state's figure for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years is $49,100, taken off assessed value before the rate is applied. At the Nelson County median value of $238,000, that leaves $188,900 to be taxed.

Apply with the Nelson County PVA, which proves age with a birth certificate, driver's license, passport or similar record. A disability-based exemption needs yearly renewal, with exceptions for veterans with service-connected disabilities and for owners found permanently and totally disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

sections.h2: What should a Nelson County seller handle about taxes before closing?
sections.html:
Kentucky treats the year's tax as a personal debt of the owner on the January 1 assessment date, and a lien follows delinquent property for eleven years under KRS 134.420. The title company will look for both.

  • Pull every bill for the parcel, including city and independent school lines if the address is inside Bardstown.
  • Check with the sheriff for the exact payoff on the day you plan to close.
  • Put the buyer's mailing address in the deed's in-care-of line for the property tax bill, as KRS 382.135 requires.
  • For an inherited house, the personal representative files an affidavit with the County Clerk listing who receives the property and its value.

If you sell a home in Bardstown or New Haven, the city bill is separate from the county bill, so a payoff that mentions only the county number leaves a gap.

faqs.q: Who do I call if my Nelson County tax bill seems too high?
faqs.a: Call the Nelson County PVA at (502) 348-1810. The sheriff's office says it never assesses property, so only the PVA can change a value.

faqs.q: Will the Nelson County Sheriff accept a payment for the wrong amount?
faqs.a: No. The sheriff returns any payment that does not match the bill exactly, including late or partial payments, because audit rules require exact accounting.

faqs.q: What happens to a Nelson County bill not paid by April 15?
faqs.a: It moves from the Sheriff's Office to the Nelson County Clerk, who handles delinquent bills after that date.

faqs.q: Do all Nelson County homeowners get the same tax bills?
faqs.a: No. Owners in districts 1, 7, 8, 11, 12 and 13 receive a county bill only, while districts 2, 3, 4, 5 and 9 also receive bills for New Haven, Bardstown, the Bardstown Independent School District or Fairfield.

faqs.q: How much is the homestead exemption in Nelson County?
faqs.a: It is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026, available to owners 65 or older or totally disabled. File with the Nelson County PVA.
